sections.name: What Was Actually in Snake Oil

lines.prompt: A flamboyant cowboy salesman in a wide hat and fringed jacket standing on a wagon stage holding up a bottle, a crowd gathered at a Wild West town

lines: In the 1890s, a cowboy called Clark Stanley became famous selling snake oil.

lines.prompt: The salesman holding a live rattlesnake up dramatically over a pot, the crowd gasping, Chicago fair setting

lines: He said he learned the recipe from healers, and boiled rattlesnakes in front of crowds.

lines.prompt: Close-up of an old glass bottle of liniment on a wooden crate, warm lantern light

lines: He claimed it cured aches, pains, toothaches and more.

lines.prompt: A 1917 government lab, a chemist in a white coat holding up a test tube, the snake oil bottle on the bench

lines: Then, in 1917, government chemists tested a bottle.

lines.prompt: Lab bench with separate dishes of mineral oil, beef fat, red chili peppers and turpentine, the chemist raising an eyebrow

lines: It was mostly mineral oil, with beef fat, red pepper and turpentine. No snake at all.

lines.prompt: A courtroom, the cowboy salesman awkwardly paying a judge a small fine, the crowd laughing

lines: He was fined twenty dollars. And snake oil became a word for any fake cure.
